question: v09
q: Has eating out got more expensive in Melbourne?

transcript.answer:
**Yes. Eating out in Melbourne keeps getting more expensive, though prices rose a bit more slowly in the latest month.**

**Latest figure (August 2026):** "Meals out and take away foods" prices in Melbourne were **3.5% higher than a year earlier**.

**How that compares:**
- **Overall Melbourne inflation** was also 3.5% in August 2026. So eating out rose at about the same pace as prices in general, not faster.
- **Nationally**, eating-out prices rose 4.1%. That means Melbourne is currently rising a little more slowly than the national average.

**Recent trend in Melbourne (year-on-year % change):**

| Period | Meals out & takeaway |
|---|---|
| Apr 2025 | 2.6% |
| Aug 2025 | 3.4% |
| Jan 2026 | 3.8% |
| May 2026 | **4.4%** (peak) |
| Jul 2026 | 4.1% |
| Aug 2026 | 3.5% |

Eating-out inflation in Melbourne sped up from around 2.3–2.6% in mid-2025 to a peak of 4.4% in May 2026, then eased to 3.5% by August. Prices are still going up, just less sharply than a few months ago. Over the past year, a meal that cost $50 would now cost about $51.75.

Source: ABS monthly Consumer Price Index, unadjusted figures, latest data for August 2026.
